vmExports.deleteDescription: The OVF files are removed from the pool. The VM stays.

dialog.title: Export {{name}} as OVA
dialog.description: The VM's disks are converted to VMware's format (VMDK) and written to a pool as an OVA package. The VM must stay off until it is written.
dialog.poolHint: The directory or NFS pool the OVA is written to. It needs as much free space as the VM's disks.
dialog.name: Name
dialog.nameHint: The name of this export and of the downloaded file. Empty uses the VM name and the time.
dialog.guestOsHint: The value VMware uses to recognise the OS (guestId, e.g. ubuntu64Guest). Empty uses the imported VM's original value, else otherGuest64.
dialog.hwVersionHint: The virtual hardware version the receiving VMware can open (7–21). 14 opens on ESXi 6.7 or later.
dialog.keepMacsHint: When on, the network cards keep their MAC addresses. Off lets the receiving product choose new ones.

errors.vm_running: Stop the VM before exporting it.
errors.pool_not_file: Choose a directory or NFS pool.
errors.insufficient_storage: The pool does not have room for the disks: {{message}}
errors.export_busy: Another task is working on this export.
errors.export_not_ready: The export is not finished yet.
errors.link_expired: The download link expired. Try again.

help.intro: VMs made into OVA files that VMware or VirtualBox can open. Start an export from a stopped VM's menu, then download it here when it is done.
help.emptyHint: Choose 'Export as OVA…' in a stopped VM's menu; it appears here and can be downloaded once written.
